alignments.note: Construct noun keeps only its own word (rule 19).
Substantival article takes the supplied 'he that' and heads on the pronoun (rule 41).

The participle is the nomen rectum, so the English possessive recasting 'hath' of the construct relation belongs here (rules 19 and 43); the unit is discontinuous around 'he that' (rule 25). The competing reading marks 'hath' added under rule 43's last clause, but the construct chain is what makes the clause possessive.

Headless relative: the written relative takes 'wherein' and the supplied antecedent 'that' goes with it (rule 46's first rider). The alternative gives 'that' to the preposition, but 'that' is a nominal and the preposition already holds 'in'.
Predicate adjective rendered by a finite verb; no separate copula is written.

review_notes: The whole verse is a verbless interrogative; 'hath' is read as the recast construct relation rather than as an added supplied verb.
